paragraphs.source_en: In this way clothing has become an exceedingly important condition for human beings, so important that one is even led to wonder: is clothing the important thing, or is man? One might almost say that human history is not the history of flesh-and-blood bodies, but the history of clothes. Therefore, when one sees a person wearing no clothes, he does not feel like a person at all, but as though one had met some monster. If all the monsters were unanimously to agree to be monsters, then the name monster would naturally disappear, and that would of course be all right. But in that case, it would only plunge human beings themselves into great perplexity. In ancient times, nature created men equal and flung them into the world. Thus, no matter what sort of person one may be, everyone is born stark naked. If human beings were content with their equal nature, they ought to have gone on living stark naked just as they were. But then one naked man came forward and said: If you, I, and everyone else are all naked alike, has not all my effort been wasted? There is simply no way to see the result of all my pains. I must devise some means by which everyone can see that I am I, and anyone who looks at me will know me at once. I want to put something on my body that will make people start in astonishment when they see it. So he spent ten years thinking up all manner of devices, and at last invented the loincloth; he put it on, strode about triumphantly, and said, “Well? Now I am something out of the ordinary, am I not?” He was the ancestor of today’s rickshaw men. Some may find it strange that a full ten years were spent merely inventing a loincloth, but that is the result of judging rashly from the present day after transporting oneself back into an age of ignorance; at the time, there was no greater invention. Descartes, it is said, took a full ten years to discover the truth that even a three-year-old understands: “I think, therefore I am.” Thinking anything out is hard work, so one must say that spending ten years to invent the loincloth was, for a rickshaw man, a most remarkable achievement. Well then! Once the loincloth had been invented, it was the rickshaw men who swaggered through the world. Then another monster appeared. Indignant that the rickshaw men, wearing loincloths, were strutting along the highways under heaven as though they owned them, he spent six years inventing the haori, that quite superfluous article. At this, the power of the loincloth at once declined, and the age of the haori reached its height. Greengrocers, apothecaries, and drapers are all latter-day descendants of this great inventor. After the age of the loincloth and the age of the haori came the age of hakama. This was devised by a monster who once flew into a rage and cried, “What is a haori, after all?” The warriors of old and the officials of today are all descendants of that breed of monster.

paragraphs.source_zh: 衣服就这样对人成了极其重要的大条件，它重要到甚至使人产生疑问：到底是衣服重要呢，还是人重要？简直可以说，人的历史不成其为血肉之躯的历史，而成了衣服的历史啦。所以一看见不穿衣服的人，就会感到这人不像人，仿佛遇上了一个怪物。如果全体怪物都一致同意做怪物，那么怪物这个称呼也就自然消失了，这当然是可以的。不过，这样一来，只能使人本身变得十分困惑。在古时候，自然平等地创造了人，把他们抛到世界上来。所以不论是什么样的人，生下来都是赤条条的。假如人安于平等的本性，那么应当就这样赤条条地生活下去。然而有一个赤条条的人出来说话啦：你我他大家都一样赤条条的，我的努力岂不是白费啦？根本看不出我费力气的结果啊。总要想个办法使所有的人都能看出我是我，谁看都能认出我。我要在身上穿点什么让别人看见都吓一跳。于是他用了十年时间想了种种办法，终于发明了裤衩，把它穿在身上，耀武扬威地到处走，并说：“怎么样？这回我可不同凡响了吧？”他就是今天人力车夫的老祖宗。只是为了发明一条裤衩就整整用了十年的岁月，有人可能觉得奇怪，其实这是从今天回过头去将自己置身于蒙昧世界加以妄断的结果，在当时说来，没有比这个更伟大的发明了。笛卡儿发现了连三岁孩子都懂得的真理：“我思，故我存”，据说他就足足用了十年的时间。思考任何一件事物都是很费力气的，所以说花费十年时间发明裤衩，对于车夫说来，应该说是十分难得的。嚯！裤衩一旦发明出来，世上趾高气扬的就是车夫。于是又出现了一个怪物，他对车夫们穿着裤衩在天下唯我独尊地横行阔步深感气愤，于是用了六年工夫发明了大褂儿这种可有可无的东西。这样一来，裤衩的势力顿时衰落，变成了大褂的全盛时代。菜铺子的老板、药铺的老板、绸布店的老板都是这个伟大发明家的末代子孙。继裤衩时期、大褂时期之后而来的是“裙裤时期”。这是一位曾大发雷霆地说“大褂又算得了什么”的怪物研究出来的，过去的武士和现在的官老爷们都是这号怪物的后代。

paragraphs.source_en: Thus the monsters vied with one another, flaunting novelty and competing in oddity, until at last even a malformed garment modeled on a swallow’s tail appeared; yet when one steps back and considers its origin, it was by no means something forced, nonsensical, accidental, or blindly cobbled together. Rather, so many new styles arose because many people, eager to outdo others, exercised their own valiant spirit; they put on all kinds of clothing to show, “I am not one of your sort.” From this state of mind, then, one great discovery can be drawn. It is this: just as nature abhors a vacuum, human beings detest equality. Today, when human beings, hating equality, cannot help but wear clothing about themselves like their very flesh, to cast aside clothing, which has become part of human essence, and return to the naked fair age of the old Mokua Ami would be the act of a madman. Even if one were willing to accept the name of madman, one could never go back. To the eyes of civilized men, those who try to go back can only be monsters. Even if all the hundreds of millions of people in the world were dragged down into the realm of monsters, and one reassured oneself that this would make things equal, since everyone would be a monster and no one need feel ashamed, it still would not do. For from the very next day after the whole world had become monsters, competition among monsters would begin again. If they could no longer compete by putting on clothes, they would compete in their condition as monsters. Let nakedness remain nakedness as much as it likes; they would still set up some other distinction. Seen from this point, clothing is, after all, something that cannot be taken off.

Rather, so many new styles arose because many people, eager to outdo others, exercised their own valiant spirit; they put on all kinds of clothing to show, “I am not one of your sort.”

paragraphs.source_zh: 这样，怪物们争先恐后、炫奇逞异，终于出现了模仿燕子尾巴的畸形服装，但退而考其由来，这可决不是勉勉强强、胡诌八扯、偶然盲目搞出来的，而是许多人为了胜过别人，发挥了自己的勇猛心，才出现了这么多的新式样，这都是为了显示我可不是你那号人才穿上种种服装的。于是，从这种心理可以引出一大发现。这就是：正如自然忌讳真空一样，人类是讨厌平等的。在今天，由于讨厌平等不得不将衣服当成毛皮一般罩在身上的今天，如果想舍掉人的本质的一部分的衣服，回到赤条条的旧阿蒙的公平时代去，那只能是狂人所为。即使有人甘冒狂人之名，也是无法倒退回去的。用文明人的眼光来看，那些想倒退回去的人只能是怪物。即使将世界上多少亿的人全部推到怪物世界中去，以为这样就可以平等，因为大家都是怪物，谁也毋需害臊了，因而觉得放心，实际上也还是不行。因为从整个世界都变成怪物的第二天起，怪物们又会开始竞争。他们如果不能用穿衣服来竞争，也会在甘居怪物的情况下搞起竞争。赤条条就让它这样赤条条下去，还会搞出另外的差别来的。由此看来，衣服毕竟是脱不得的。

paragraphs.source_en: And yet the group of people now spread out before my eyes had stripped off every last thing that ought not to be stripped off, loincloths, haori, and hakama alike, and with no reserve at all, under the gaze of all around, exposed their original ugliness in naked form, chatting and laughing as unconcernedly as could be. This is what I meant a little while ago by a truly extraordinary spectacle. I regard it as the highest honor to introduce their condition here for the benefit of civilized gentlemen.
